root.note: Further back the trail is unclear. Several sources take Arabic ruzz from Greek óruza; Corominas only says both seem to come from India. Beyond that scholars debate an Iranian language, Sanskrit or Tamil.

history: Paella starts with an Arabic word. Arabic ruzz with its article gave ar-ruzz, ‘the rice’, and Andalusian Arabic passed that to Spanish, article included: the a- and double r of arroz come from Arabic ar-. Rice has a long road behind it. Greek had óruza, and several sources say Arabic ruzz came from it. Both seem to go back further East. Scholars link them to Persian, to Sanskrit vrīhi and even to Tamil, but no route is secure, so we leave that part open. Italian took riso through its own channels, and from Italy came French riz and English rice. These words share an ancestor with arroz, but not its Arabic ‘the’.
historyEinfach: Arroz means ‘rice’. Spanish took it from Arabic. In Arabic, ar-ruzz means ‘the rice’. So the a- at the start of arroz is the Arabic word for ‘the’. Before that, the word came from the East, but experts don't agree on the road. English rice and French riz are related to it.

elsewhere.text: Say ar-ruzz aloud and you are very close to arroz.
English came by the Greek and Italian road, so it has no article inside it.
Italian took the word from Greek, not from Arabic.
French took the word from Italian.
